correctness.rationale: Rule184 transports each occupied site clockwise only to a vacant next site; for k<=n/2, periodicity is equivalent to absence of cyclic 11 and any remaining occupied pair at time t corresponds to a strictly positive preimage prefix of length 2t+2. Because 2(t+1)<=2m<=n in relevant t<=m-1, the backward cone has no repeated sites. First return of the excursion to height zero yields a primitive positive Dyck block of semilength >=t+2, and conversely every such block creates a later jam. Cyclic noncrossing bracket matching uniquely decomposes each word into singleton zeros and primitive Dyck blocks, with coefficients C_(j-1); a cycle of r atoms contributes n/r times its ordered atom generating function, including rotational stabilizers. Therefore the finite logarithm gives every mass-specific labelled R(t); particle-hole duality handles k>n/2, and at k=0 or n the first-entry T=0 sector count equals 1. The maximal new block semilength m yields exactly nC_(m-1). Independent bitmask Rule184 simulation and exact rational cyclic atom counts agree for n=2..12, 183 (n,k,t) CDF comparisons. A finite census does not prove arbitrary n; the local-preimage plus unique circular matching argument does.
